docs.article:
Floor plan to 3D home#

Upload the floor plan from a project brochure and get a furnished 3D home in about a minute. Buyers can walk through it on their phone, and you can share it on WhatsApp.

You need: the plan as a PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF. A screenshot of the brochure page is fine. Any hints you add (carpet area, BHK) make it more accurate.

Make one#

  1. Open the app (/app) and press Floor plan → 3D on the upload screen.
  2. Pick the plan image. Optionally add:
    • Carpet area (sq ft): the most useful hint, because it sets the scale. Built-up and super built-up areas work too; say which one it is.
    • Plan width (m): the outside width of the flat, if you know it. This wins over the area.
    • BHK: caps how many rooms are called bedrooms.
    • Style: Modern Indian, Scandinavian, Luxury or Minimal. This sets the floors, wall paint, wood and fabrics.
    • City and Name: used for the title and the share message.
  3. Press Read plan. After a few seconds the plan comes back as a drawing, with each room coloured by type, its name and its area.
  4. Check it:
    • Tap a room to rename it or change its type (Bedroom, Kitchen, Pooja room…).
    • Rotate 90° or Flip if the plan was read sideways or mirrored. The entrance door is drawn in green, with a green IN marker.
    • Doors. Doors the reader added (the plan didn't show them) are highlighted in orange. Press Edit doors and tap a wall to add a 0.9 m door. Tap a door, window or open gap to switch it between the three, remove it or make it the entrance. Tap IN, then a door or an outside wall, to move the entrance. Every change re-checks that each room can be reached and names the ones that can't. **Add doors for me** adds the fewest doors that connect them. With the keyboard, openings and the IN marker are buttons. In Edit doors a room's panel lists + Door to … for each neighbouring room.
  5. Press Generate 3D home. When it is ready you get the link, an Open button, Share on WhatsApp and Copy link.

The link opens standing at the entrance of the living room. There is one hotspot per room with its name and area, and a short guided tour through the rooms.

What it builds#

  • Walls at 3 m with real openings. Doors are 2.1 m high and drawn open, so you can walk through. Windows run from a 0.9 m sill to 2.1 m and have frames and glass.
  • Floors, ceilings and skirting. Floor materials follow the room type: tiles in bathrooms and the kitchen, outdoor tiles on balconies, wood or marble elsewhere, depending on the style.
  • One ceiling light per room.

  • Furniture by room type:

    RoomFurniture
    Livingsofa, coffee table, TV unit, rug
    Bedroombed, side tables, wardrobe
    Kitchencounter, fridge
    Diningtable, chairs
    BathroomWC, vanity, shower
    Studydesk, chair
    Poojamandir unit
    Balconychairs, table
    Utilitywashing machine
    Foyershoe rack

    Furniture stands against a wall. It stays out of door swings and keeps a 0.75 m walkway, and no two pieces overlap. A piece that does not fit is left out; nothing is squeezed in.

  • Before publishing, the generator walks the home on a 10 cm grid, starting at the entrance. If any room cannot be reached, it does not publish. Instead it names the room, and the plan editor highlights it (usually a door that was read as a window, or a wall that was read through a doorway).

How well it reads plans#

Two readers are used:

  • The plan reader always runs. It needs no AI and no network. It finds the walls (solid, grey or hatched), the gaps in them, and the rooms between them. A gap whose lines run along it is a window; a gap with a drawn door leaf is a door. Measured on the test set (6 flats from 1 to 4 BHK, each drawn in 3 brochure styles — clean, tinted with furniture, and a noisy hatched scan):

    MeasuredTarget
    Wall overlap (IoU)0.86≥ 0.85
    Rooms found95 %≥ 90 %
    Doors92 %≥ 85 %
    Windows94 %≥ 85 %
    Scale error, no hints2.4 %≤ 5 %
    Room types, no AI67 %≥ 60 %

    The reader cannot read text, so it guesses room types from size and layout. For example, the biggest room the entrance opens into is the living room, and small closed rooms are toilets.

  • The AI reader runs only when the operator has turned it on (see below). It reads the labels printed on the plan ("M. BED", "TOI", "KIT", "POOJA"), the dimension text (feet-and-inches or metres) and the entrance. Where the plan reader's rooms agree with the AI's, the plan reader's geometry is kept and the AI supplies names and types. Where they disagree (photos, colour-filled brochures, line drawings), the plan is built from the AI's rooms. The scale comes from the printed room dimensions, measured against the room outlines in pixels.

    Measured with the real Anthropic API (claude-haiku-5-5, the default) on 28 plans. 18 are the synthetic test plans above. 10 are brochure-style plans made for the test: a colour brochure, a tinted plan with wood floors and a watermark, a line drawing, a "SAMPLE FLAT" watermark, a low-resolution plan in metres, a large 4 BHK, two phone photos of the printed page (turned 4° and 7°, keystoned, uneven light), a turned noisy scan, and a two-unit page. These are rooms found, room types right, doors, windows, wall overlap and scale error:

    PlansReaderRoomsTypesDoorsWindowsWallsScale error
    Synthetic, clean (6)Plan reader96 %71 %94 %100 %0.882 %
    AI only100 %100 %74 %66 %0.682 %
    Both99 %100 %94 %100 %0.87< 0.5 %
    Synthetic, tinted (6)Plan reader96 %71 %94 %100 %0.852 %
    AI only100 %100 %96 %98 %0.771 %
    Both99 %100 %94 %100 %0.881 %
    Synthetic, scan (6)Plan reader94 %59 %88 %83 %0.833 %
    AI only100 %100 %59 %55 %0.721 %
    Both99 %100 %88 %90 %0.811 %
    Brochure-style (10)Plan reader49 %29 %51 %46 %0.35152 %
    AI only100 %100 %67 %66 %0.561 %
    Both99 %100 %94 %93 %0.561 %
    All 28Plan reader79 %53 %77 %77 %0.6856 %
    AI only100 %100 %73 %71 %0.661 %
    Both99 %100 %93 %96 %0.751 %

    Per brochure-style plan, with both readers: every plan has 91–100 % of its rooms and 100 % of its types, and every one builds (the walk reaches every room). The weak spots are the phone photos (77–93 % of the doors, 78–83 % of the windows). The plan reader alone cannot read the line drawing, the metric plan, the wood-floor plan or the two photos at all.

    Doors the readers miss. A missed door leaves a room nobody can walk into, and the build refuses the plan. So before the plan is shown, the reader checks it the way the build does and adds the most likely door for every room that can't be reached: on a wall the room shares with a room you can reach, chosen by what the two rooms are (a toilet opens off the passage or a bedroom, not the living room or the kitchen; a pooja room off the living room or the foyer; one attached toilet per bedroom), at a standard width (0.75 m toilet, 0.8 m kitchen, 0.9 m bedroom, 1.2 m balcony), where the AI marked a door if it marked one near there. A page with two flats gets a front door per flat. Where the plan came from the AI's reading, a living room, bedroom, kitchen or toilet with no window gets one in the middle of its outside wall. Doors added this way are flagged added: true in the plan and highlighted on the edit step.

    Open plans. A kitchen open to the living room is drawn as a counter line, and an archway as a gap with thin lines across it. Readers used to take both for windows, which cut the rooms behind them off. Now a "window" between a living room / dining / kitchen and a kitchen / passage is an open gap (kind: "open": no leaf, walked through like a doorway). One between a bedroom and a living room or passage is a door. A doorway of 1 m or more between a kitchen / living / dining and a living / dining / passage is an open gap too. On the AI's own geometry, where every room is outlined, a kitchen, dining or living room whose outline touches another's gets an open gap between them. The plan reader also re-searches wall gaps at the door scale (thin-walled drawings used to leak 2 m openings into the outside). It closes a wide window (up to 4.2 m) that encloses a room, and it puts the entrance on the living room's outside door.

    The repair. If a room still can't be reached, each cut-off part of the plan gets one door. It goes on the longest wall that part shares with the reachable rooms, choosing a believable pair first: a bedroom off the passage or the living room, a utility off the kitchen, and the living room, dining, passage, kitchen or foyer as the usual way in. Doors never go through a bathroom and never in an outside wall. A wrong entrance is moved to the living room's outside door first. Only a room no legal door can reach is left for the owner (the build's 422 names it). /v1/plan2home/analyze reports repair: { added, entrance, unreachable }. Before this, 6 of the 10 brochure-style plans could not be built, and doors / windows were 84 % / 77 % on them (89 % / 88 % on all 28).

    Real plans (16 Oct). Production met real plans the test set did not have — 376 px brochure crops, colour-filled CAD exports, US listing plans with furniture in orange and blue, walls drawn as a grey fill between two outlines, tiled toilets, one image that was not a plan at all. Changes:

    • The plan reader reads a plan up to four ways and keeps the most plausible reading (rooms cover the outline, none swallows the plan, few slivers, every room reachable): the classic reading; one that ignores coloured fills (furniture, wood floors) for the walls but still reads blue window and brown railing lines; one for dark walls only (grey floors and tiles are not walls); and one for light-grey walls between two outlines. Small images are scaled up first. The door scale now comes from gaps that have a drawn leaf or swing, clustered by width, so a thick-walled drawing no longer hides its doors. It also finds doors between two wall ends with no wall along the door line, window glass drawn on the wall line, balconies fenced by railings, and seals wide sliding doors that left a room open to the outside.
    • The AI reader is told what real sheets hold (open kitchens with no wall, arches, furniture and tiles that are not walls, printed room areas, a total on the sheet, images that are not plans). It reports printed room areas, which set the scale when there are no dimensions. The merge fuses rooms the plan reader split (a bed or a label read as a wall), keeps the floor the model's outlines leave out, and re-reads every door's two rooms. A plan reader reading that looks implausible is not merged at all.
    • Validation before build. Every reading is checked: the rooms' total against the printed total or your carpet-area hint (15 %), each room against its printed area or dimensions, overlapping doors or rooms, rooms under 1.5 m² that are not a toilet or store, and rooms nobody can reach. Slivers join their neighbour, a balcony read a little off the wall is moved to it, a wall read twice keeps one door, and the front door is an outside door into the foyer / living / dining (added if the plan shows none). If the AI's reading still fails, the plan is read again by claude-sonnet-5-5, then claude-opus-5-5, each told what was wrong; the reading with the fewest problems wins (ai.tries). Whatever is still off is listed in Check rooms ("Check before you build"), each item selecting its room — never a dead end.
    • Not a plan: a photo of a room is refused with a message, not built.
    • The walkthrough plans again with tighter margins when a narrow hall with doors swung into it closed the walk.

    Measured on 13 real plans (private; their truth was written by reading each image) with web/test/fix-verify-ih-real.mjs: see the CHANGELOG for the table. The gate also runs against staging, where the AI reader is on (IH_BASE, IH_GATE).

    Speed and cost (Anthropic list prices): one AI read takes 12 s (median; 15 s at the 90th percentile, 19 s at worst). It uses about 5,400 input and 2,600 output tokens, which is $0.002 per plan. claude-sonnet-5-5 scored the same on rooms and types, lower on doors (86 %) and windows (89 %), took 8 s, and cost $0.023 per plan (12 × more). If Haiku's answer cannot be used, the reader asks claude-opus-5-5 once. On the four hardest plans, Opus found 92–100 % of the doors, against 27–73 % for Haiku. It costs $0.07 per plan and takes 13–26 s. In the test, no Haiku answer needed this retry.

    The eval is web/test/plan2home/ai-eval.mjs. It replays the recorded answers offline, and the plan2home gate enforces the numbers above with a margin.

Known limits#

  • Walls must be horizontal or vertical. A diagonal wall is read as steps or skipped.
  • One floor per upload. Duplexes and villas need one upload per floor.
  • With no hint and no printed number, the scale comes from the doors (a typical door is 0.85–0.9 m), which can be 15 % off; with the AI reader, a scale that makes the bedrooms implausible is replaced by a typical bedroom size. Add the carpet area for a better result.
  • Without the AI reader, room types are guessed from size and layout: kitchens, utilities, stores and passages are often mislabelled. Rename them in Check rooms.
  • A sheet with two flats is read as both flats and their lobby.
  • Without the AI reader, photographed, colour-filled and line-drawn plans are often not read. With it, a photo turned a few degrees (tested up to 7°) is straightened and read, but its doors and windows are less reliable than a flat scan's. Colourful 3D renders are not read well. Use the 2D plan page of the brochure.

Privacy#

The plan image stays on the server that you upload to. **The image is sent to the Anthropic API only when the operator has set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY**, and then only so the AI reader can read the labels. Without the key, nothing leaves the server. The server log records the request size and timing, but never the image or the AI's answer.

Operator setup#

VariableDefaultWhat it does
ANTHROPIC_API_KEYunsetTurns on the AI reader. Without it, only the plan reader runs.
VERSE_PLAN_MODELclaude-haiku-5-5The model the AI reader uses. If it is overloaded or down, the reader tries claude-sonnet-5-5 once (or claude-haiku-5-5 if another model is set).
VERSE_PLAN_RETRY_MODELclaude-opus-5-5Asked once when the first model's answer cannot be used. off turns the retry off.
VERSE_PLAN_ESCALATEclaude-sonnet-5-5,claude-opus-5-5Read the plan again with these models, in order, when a reading fails validation (areas off, rooms unreachable, overlapping doors, impossible rooms). off turns it off.
VERSE_PLAN_ESCALATE_MS50000No new reading starts after this long.
VERSE_PLAN_PROMPTv3The prompt version (v2, v1 for comparison).
VERSE_PLAN_EFFORTmediumEffort for the AI reader. low is about twice as fast, and finds fewer doors and windows (83 % and 82 %).
VERSE_PLAN_TIMEOUT_MS60000The longest the AI reader may take, including a retry. After that, the plan reader's result is used.
VERSE_PLAN_DAILY_CAP500AI reads per server per day.
VERSE_PLAN_LIB_DIRtools/plan2home-libThe CC0 furniture and material library (optional).

The furniture and material library is optional. It is not in the repository: run node tools/plan2home-lib/fetch.mjs to download it. The fetch checks every file against the manifest. Without the library, the furniture is built from simple shapes and the materials are flat colours. Sources and licences are listed in Attributions.

The API is described in the API reference.
